clue.text: Undertakes to use idiots without hesitation

indicators.note: here without means outside, so the word for idiots wraps round the hesitation

parts.note: asses are fools or idiots
um is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone takes on the job of employing fools, and does it without hesitating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense 'outside': UM sits inside ASSES.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume a name or manner is to take it on and adopt it for one's own employment.

clue.text: Endlessly serving out tropical fruit

indicators.note: serving out suggests dishing up in a different order, so the trimmed letters are rearranged
endlessly tells us to drop the final letter of the word tropical

explanation.surface: A waiter keeps dishing up exotic fruit without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' removes the L from 'tropical', leaving TROPICA, which 'serving out' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An apricot is an orange stone fruit, so it is an example of the general term.

clue.text: Barred entry to small shed in the garden

parts.note: a hut is a small shed
being in the garden is being outdoors, out of the house

explanation.surface: Someone was locked out of the little shed at the bottom of the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: To shut someone out is to keep them from coming in, denying them admission.

clue.text: I object to fish served up with red wine

parts.note: the object form of I is me

indicators.note: in a down clue served up means the word is read upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: cod is a fish

explanation.surface: A diner protests at fish being brought with a red rather than white wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I object' means I in the object case: ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Médoc is a Bordeaux district whose claret is a well-known red.

clue.text: Youth by net always supports linesman

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece that supports sits underneath the others

parts.note: a son is a youth or young man
taken as written
e'er is the poetic short form of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A young player by the tennis net is always backed up by the line judge.
explanation.walkthrough: A linesman here is a writer of lines of verse, not a sports official.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonneteer composes poems in lines, so he is jokingly one who makes lines.

clue.text: Drop by to get a batter pudding

definitions.meaning: to drop by is to call in on someone briefly
a light hollow baked item made from egg batter, like a Yorkshire pudding

explanation.surface: Call in on a friend and be given a Yorkshire-style pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: To pop over is to make a quick visit; a popover is also an American batter muffin, puffed and hollow.

clue.text: Do get an accessory!

definitions.meaning: a do is a social gathering or celebration
an accessory to a crime is a ... to it

explanation.surface: Buy a fashion accessory to wear to the event.
explanation.definitionFit: A do is a festive gathering, and someone involved in a crime is a participant or accomplice.

clue.text: I get cuddled by girl in light bed

indicators.note: in places the girl and her contents inside the word for light

parts.note: pale means light in colour

indicators.note: being cuddled means being held inside someone's arms, so one piece is wrapped round the other

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Someone is hugged by a young woman in a pale-coloured bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A palliasse is a straw-filled mattress, a simple kind of sleeping place.

clue.text: The ABC of nutrition?

parts.note: the ABC is not the basics of the subject but the letters A, B and C naming dietary essentials

explanation.definitionFit: A, B and C are each named dietary micronutrients the body needs.

clue.text: Resumption of music makes agent get up

parts.note: a rep is a sales agent or representative
to rise is to get up

explanation.surface: A theme returning in a piece makes the sales representative stand up.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a reprise is a repeat of an earlier passage or theme.

clue.text: Ring number back to retaliate verbally

parts.note: a round is a ring or circle

indicators.note: back means the abbreviation is read in reverse

explanation.surface: Someone rings a number back in order to give the caller an earful.
explanation.definitionFit: To round on someone is to turn and attack them with angry words.

clue.text: A little bread on lid of desk

indicators.note: on means the first piece comes before, sitting on, the second in an across answer

parts.note: a roll is a small piece of bread
a top is a lid

explanation.surface: Breadcrumbs from a small loaf sit on the lid of an office desk.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll-top is a writing bureau with a flexible slatted cover that slides up.

clue.text: Irritable note written by Yemeni leader

parts.note: a crotchet is a musical note, a quarter note

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Yemeni ruler pens a bad-tempered memo.
explanation.definitionFit: Crotchety describes someone grumpy and cantankerous, easily annoyed.

clue.text: I confront a GP putting iodine on feet

indicators.note: to confront is to stand before, so I is placed first

parts.note: taken as written
a GP is a doctor, and MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A patient faces the doctor, who applies iodine to their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: The feet are metrical feet in verse, not body parts.
explanation.definitionFit: An iamb is a metrical unit of verse, short then long, so its plural names poetic units of rhythm.

clue.text: Second French person to run into a coach

parts.note: tu is the French second-person singular pronoun
taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Another Frenchman sprints to catch a bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second person' is grammar: in French the familiar 'you' is TU. 'into a' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor is a private teacher who coaches a pupil.

clue.text: Retinue in repose shows self-control

indicators.note: in places the retinue inside the word for repose

parts.note: rest is repose
a train is the retinue of attendants following an important person

explanation.surface: A royal entourage at rest displays admirable composure.
explanation.definitionFit: Restraint is self-discipline, holding back one's impulses.

clue.text: Always wrong the church thereafter

parts.note: ever means always
a sin is a wrong
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: The church has been in error all along.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever since means from that time onwards, continuously after that.

clue.text: English designer unusually full of vigour

indicators.note: unusually means the letters of designer are arranged in a non-standard order

explanation.surface: An English fashion designer is remarkably lively.
explanation.definitionFit: Energised means invigorated, filled with energy and pep.

clue.text: Bar demands money before admitting one

parts.note: brass is slang for money

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A bar insists on payment before it will let anyone in.
explanation.definitionFit: A brasserie is an informal café-restaurant serving drinks and food.

clue.text: Bungler gets many into trouble

indicators.note: into means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: bother is trouble
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a lot

explanation.surface: A clumsy person lands lots of others in difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: A botcher is someone who does a job clumsily, making a mess of it.

clue.text: Supplement with a sprinkling of nutmeg

indicators.note: a sprinkling scatters the letters of a and nutmeg into a new order

explanation.surface: A recipe tip: add a dusting of nutmeg as an extra.
explanation.definitionFit: To augment is to add to or enlarge, the same as to top up.

clue.text: French apathy

parts.note: the clue asks for the French-borrowed word for listless weariness

explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless boredom, a word borrowed from French.

clue.text: Oh dear! Nick was upset by her

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: ah is an exclamation of dismay
Old Nick is a name for the devil, Satan

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in dismay that a thief was rattled by a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was upset' turns AH + SATAN round to give NATAS + HA.
explanation.definitionFit: Natasha is a woman's name, so it stands for a female person.

clue.text: Fashionable collection able to be viewed

parts.note: in means fashionable
a range is a collection of products

explanation.surface: A trendy clothing line is on display.
explanation.definitionFit: In range means within reach of sight or of an instrument, so it can be seen.

clue.text: Woods harbouring a wild animal

definitions.meaning: a large striped big cat of the jungle

explanation.surface: A forest shelters a dangerous beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The golfer Woods has this first name, and the big striped cat is a wild beast.

clue.text: Urge game assistant to get kitchen utensil

parts.note: to egg on is to urge
on a shoot a beater helps by flushing out the game birds

explanation.surface: Encourage the shoot's helper to fetch a whisk.
explanation.walkthrough: In British game shooting, beaters drive birds towards the guns.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg beater is a hand whisk used for cooking.

clue.text: Desperate for time in HM's presence

indicators.note: in places the time inside the royal letters

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the monarch, Her Majesty
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone longs for a moment with the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the old Queen's cipher, Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: Being eager for something is being keen and longing to have it.

clue.text: Improbable odds?

parts.note: ironic: a one-to-one chance is anything but unlikely, which is the joke

explanation.definitionFit: Evens are betting odds of one to one, a fifty-fifty chance.

clue.text: Listing is a job for the cobbler

definitions.meaning: a ship that is listing is leaning to one side
a shoe mender fits new parts on the backs of shoes

explanation.surface: Tilting over is all in a day's work for the shoe mender.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat tilting to one side is said to heel; a cobbler also puts new heels on shoes.

clue.text: Poles consume pesto made by one of the family

indicators.note: to consume is to take in, so the poles surround the rest

parts.note: S and N are the south and north poles

indicators.note: made suggests the letters of pesto are made into something new

explanation.surface: Polish people eat pesto that a relative has made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges PESTO to TEPSO, which sits between S and N.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepson is a spouse's son from an earlier relationship, a relative by marriage.

clue.text: Taking rubbish to a hill requires muscle

parts.note: rot is rubbish or nonsense
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Carrying the trash up a hillside needs strength.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotator is a muscle that turns a limb or body part about its axis.

clue.text: Sickness in seaside resort

indicators.note: resort is read as re-sort, sorting the letters of seaside again

explanation.surface: Illness strikes a holiday town by the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Disease is illness, a disorder of the body.
